title: Read Each Branch as a Number
statement:
Every node of a binary tree holds a single digit from 0 to 9. Walk from the root down to a leaf and write the digits in order: that path spells a number. The path 3 → 0 → 7 spells 307.

Return the sum of the numbers spelled by all root-to-leaf paths. A leaf is a node with no children; a node with one child is not the end of a path.

examples.why: A zero in the middle is still a digit: 207 + 203 = 410.
Only the bottom 0 is a leaf. Counting the root or the middle node as a path end would add 1 and 10 by mistake.

hints: Going one level down turns the number so far, say 30, into 30 × 10 + digit. What do you need to carry into each recursive call?
Pass the number spelled so far down the tree. At a leaf, that number is complete.
DFS with a running value: value = value × 10 + node.val. Return it at a leaf, and the sum of both children's results otherwise. Skip missing children rather than treating them as leaves.

explain.intuition:
Writing a digit at the end of a number is the same as multiplying by 10 and adding the digit. So each node only needs the number spelled by its ancestors: it multiplies it by 10, adds its own digit, and hands the result to its children.

The only subtle part is where a path ends. It ends at a leaf, not at a missing child. If a node has one child, it is in the middle of a path, and its partial number must not be counted on its own.
steps: If node is null, return 0: no path goes through here.
pitfalls: Adding cur when you reach a null child. A node with one child would then count its partial number, as in [1, null, 0, null, 0].
Building strings and parsing them at the end. It works but is slower and hides the simple arithmetic.
Skipping zeros because they "add nothing". A 0 in the middle still shifts the digits: 2→0→7 is 207, not 27.

complexity.space: O(h) for the recursion, h = tree height

solutions.title: Recursive DFS with a running number
solutions.idea: Carry the number spelled so far. At a leaf return it; otherwise return the sum from both subtrees.

solutions.title: Iterative with an explicit stack
solutions.idea: Push (node, number so far) pairs. Pop one, extend the number, and either add it to the total at a leaf or push the children.

followups: Do it with O(1) extra space. (Hint: Morris traversal, undoing the multiplication when you climb back up a thread.)
The digits are now in base 2. What changes, and could you use bit operations?
